q: Comprising 30 diverse learning tasks and 13 unseen transfer tasks, EngramBench challenges agents to navigate interactive, multi-hour development cycles driven by LLM-simulated users.
r: Include b: a benchmark of multi-hour development tasks evaluating skill banks (procedural memory) for a coding agent, a context mechanism with controlled ablation.

q: Central to the performance of these agents is the coding rules file, often instantiated as an AGENTS.md document and prepended to the backbone model’s input context
r: Include b: coding rules files (AGENTS.md) for coding agents are the object, evaluated across agent frameworks and models.

q: We introduce TokenEconomizer, an external controller that learns environment-specific policies for micro-skill activation, tool pruning, and failure-loop intervention.
r: EC5: a new external cost controller tested on SWE-bench and other existing benchmarks; the evaluation method is not the contribution.

q: This raises two questions: can the agent still solve the task, and does it still respect the rules it was given?
r: Include c: controlled empirical comparison of context-compaction strategies for coding agents on project-level tasks (ProgramBench), including rule retention.

q: We ran Claude Code on 30 SWE-bench Verified issues, qualitatively coded the 125 proposals from /retro, implemented 24, and evaluated 12 harness changes on later issues from the same repositories
r: Include b: study of how Claude Code harness changes (CLAUDE.md, skills, instructions) proposed by /retro affect later sessions.

q: Our study systematically explores the effects of deleting content from old turns by varying the scope, granularity, amount, and timing of deletion across 9,400 runs with two state-of-theart agents on the SWE-bench Verified dataset.
r: EC6: empirical study of trajectory reduction on SWE-bench Verified, which is issue repair.

q: We analyzed the initial instruction stacks of 1,886 releases across five coding agents.
r: Include b: analyses the instruction stacks (system prompts and instructions) of five coding agents and their evolution.

q: The model must regenerate the masked region and is never told that the task is security-relevant
r: EC6: security of generated code on masked-region tasks, not feature or project level development.

q: We evaluate Claude Code with Haiku 4.5 against a raw-tool baseline on four repository-level tasks: fault localization with LinuxFLBench, repository-level code generation and repair with SWE-bench Pro, test generation with SWT-bench, and security patching with SecBench.
r: EC6: tasks are fault localization, repair, test generation and security patching, not application development.

q: We train CAMP-II-4B and CAMP-II-9B from Qwen3.5 models of matching size.
r: EC5: a new memory-distillation training method and environments for agents, tested on Terminal-Bench and SWE-Bench Pro, adding nothing to the evaluation method.
